topTool.defaultPrompt:
Use the uploaded image as the only visual reference. Identify the clearest main subject, object, person, product, pet, plant, room detail, or visual fragment, then reinterpret that subject as a quiet minimal zine poster rather than copying the original photo exactly.

Create a paper-poster composition that follows the output canvas selected on the page. Use full-frame aged off-white paper, 70% to 90% calm negative space, and one small visual cluster occupying about 8% to 25% of the canvas. Place the cluster away from the edges, preferably center, upper-middle, lower-left, or upper-right. Do not force an alternate crop or nested frame.

Treat the subject as a tiny faded photo crop, torn-paper clipping, flat silhouette, old printed illustration, object specimen, or paper texture window. Blend it into the paper using xerox softness, halftone wear, risograph grain, scan noise, paper fibers, subtle ink bleed, and slight misregistration. Keep the main subject recognizable, but make the final image feel regenerated as archival print design.

Add sparse serif, typewriter, or monospaced microtype with one very short readable phrase and optional tiny date or archive marks. Use one unmistakably saturated high-chroma ink accent, such as cobalt blue, ultramarine, tomato red, lemon yellow, pear green, cyan, violet, or orange. The accent should be a visible printed block, cutout, subject fragment, or type element occupying about 0.8% to 2.5% of the whole canvas or 15% to 35% of the small cluster.

Keep the whole image flat like a scanned paper sheet with matte absorbent texture, diffuse light, low-to-medium contrast, and a quiet Japanese or Korean indie editorial zine mood. Avoid full-bleed scenes, commercial headlines, logo lockups, CTA layout, glossy mockups, clean digital UI white, cinematic lighting, 3D depth, neon, cute cartoon style, dense scrapbook collage, too many colors, and long clean text blocks.

hero.desc: Upload one image and turn its main subject into a quiet paper-poster composition. Toolaze uses a minimal zine style with aged texture, sparse typography, large negative space, and one vivid ink accent.

intro.title: What This Zine Poster Generator Creates

content.title: A quiet poster from a single photo
content.text: The generator reads the uploaded image, finds the clearest subject, and turns it into a zine-style paper poster. The output is not a literal copy of the photo. It is a regenerated paper composition with a small focal cluster, archival texture, and a restrained editorial mood.

content.title: No writing required
content.text: You do not need to write style directions. Upload one image, choose the available output settings, and generate. The zine-poster style logic handles subject placement, paper texture, sparse type, and the color accent automatically.

howToUse.title: How to Turn a Photo Into a Zine Poster

steps.title: Upload one image
steps.desc: Choose a photo with a clear person, product, object, pet, plant, room detail, or visual subject.

steps.title: Choose the output shape
steps.desc: Select the aspect ratio you want before generating. The zine style adapts to that canvas while keeping the subject airy.

steps.title: Generate and download
steps.desc: Create the poster, review the subject, texture, type, and color accent, then download the result.

items.title: Large Negative Space
items.desc: The subject stays small so the paper surface, silence, and composition become part of the image.

items.title: Recognizable Subject Anchor
items.desc: The uploaded person, product, pet, plant, object, or room detail remains readable as the tiny focal point.

items.title: Aged Paper Texture
items.desc: Soft scan noise, halftone wear, paper fibers, and ink bleed create an analog editorial feel.

items.title: Sparse Typography
items.desc: Tiny serif, typewriter, or monospaced marks add a zine-cover rhythm without becoming a headline.

items.title: Quiet Editorial Mood
items.desc: The result stays calm, flat, and indie-poster-like instead of turning into a glossy ad or full scene.

items.title: One Vivid Ink Accent
items.desc: A single saturated color, such as cobalt, tomato red, lemon yellow, or pear green, keeps the poster readable at a glance.

photoTips.title: Best Photos to Upload
photoTips.subtitle: The style works best when the main subject is easy to recognize before the image is transformed.

items.title: Use one clear subject
items.desc: A product, face, flower, chair, pet, shoe, book, or small object usually works better than a crowded scene.

items.title: Keep the edges visible
items.desc: Avoid heavy cropping, covered outlines, or motion blur when the shape of the subject matters.

items.title: Simple backgrounds help
items.desc: Busy photos can still work, but cleaner backgrounds make it easier to choose the subject and simplify the poster.

items.title: Do not rely on tiny text
items.desc: The zine style is strongest for shape, mood, texture, and color. Small logos, labels, and fine text may change.

faq.q: Do I need to write a prompt?
faq.a: No. Upload one image and Toolaze applies the zine-poster style automatically.

faq.q: Will the output copy my photo exactly?
faq.a: No. The generator keeps the main subject recognizable, but the final image is regenerated as a minimal paper poster with new texture, layout, and type.
Use a clear photo with one main subject, visible edges, and enough contrast for the object or person to be recognized.

faq.q: Can I use this for product or brand visuals?
faq.a: Yes, it can help create moodboards, social visuals, poster drafts, and editorial concepts. Review final outputs before commercial use, especially if your upload includes logos, people, or protected assets.
